content.content:
An operation is one whole creation, one whole recording, or one whole removal, and only those three bracket. A registry write is none of the three: it creates no node and no change, records no edit into a node, and removes neither. A registry write is therefore not an operation, is never bracketed, and is never undone or redone: undo and redo step whole operations, and a registry write is not one.

Landing a draft is the recording it already is — the operation the vocabulary already names. For every landing, that recording marks the draft's record `landed` and retains it. That record update is partial work inside the recording: not a second operation, and not separately bracketed.

These are one commitment: the registry is outside the operation vocabulary, and the landing update is part of the recording, not an operation of its own. The first two clauses keep the registry out of the operation set: nothing done to the registry is itself an operation. The last two put the one moment the registry is touched during a recorded operation inside that operation, not beside it. Neither half stands alone. If a registry write could be an operation, the landing update would be a second operation beside the recording, and undo would step each of them as its own unit; if the landing update stood beside the recording, the registry would have entered the operation set through the one door the first half closes. So the clauses are not separately decidable: each half is what makes the other true, and the boundary is drawn once.
content.rationale:
The boundary has an inside and an outside, and it is one decision because the outside is what leaves the inside a single place.

Outside: an operation is one whole creation, recording, or removal (lmwpuqlx), and only those three bracket (vwlrqoxk), so the vocabulary is closed and there is no fourth form a registry write could take. That a registry write is none of the three follows from the record itself: the record is not a node and not a change (owyntkvw), so writing it creates nothing the graph holds, records no edit into a node, and removes nothing. 'Never bracketed' and 'never undone or redone' then follow rather than being added beside the definition: bracketing belongs to the three mutating invocations (vwlrqoxk), and undo and redo are defined over whole operations (prsoxsuo), so a thing that is not an operation offers them no unit to step. No separate rule is made for registry writes; there is simply nothing there for a rule about operations to reach.

Inside: landing is a recording (rvyrosmp), and landing is per draft (znskspqs), so a draft's landing is the recording of that draft's named edits into its node's change. That recording is already an operation of the vocabulary, so nothing new has to be introduced for the record update to have a home. The draft's record is marked `landed` and kept when the draft lands (vkkwusty): that is the state the transition ends in, retained at that end. Because the update happens within that one recording, it is partial work inside an operation, which the operation definition already refuses to count as an operation (lmwpuqlx); and because it is not an operation, it never brackets apart from the recording it rides in (vwlrqoxk).

So the two halves are the same cut. Suppose a registry write could be an operation: then the landing update would have to stand as a second operation beside the recording, and undoing the landing would have to reverse it separately — which is the opposite of the first half. Suppose instead the landing update stood beside the recording: then the registry would have entered the operation set through the one moment it is touched, which is the opposite of the first half too. Both statements hold only together, so no clause can be decided, changed, or dropped while the others stay as they are.

All seven prerequisites are load-bearing and named. owyntkvw supplies the object a registry write would otherwise have to be, and that it is neither a node nor a change. vkkwusty supplies the `landed` state and its retention, which is what the landing update applies. lmwpuqlx and vwlrqoxk supply the closed vocabulary and what brackets. prsoxsuo supplies the unit undo and redo step, and that undoing a recording restores the prior file state, so a second unit beside the recording would not be undoable as part of the same step. rvyrosmp supplies the operation that landing already is, and znskspqs supplies landing being per draft, which is why one recording carries its own draft's record update.

A cap on open records, a barrier over them, the command surface that would report them, and the verb surface for registry writes are separate commitments decided elsewhere; so is what the record's state vocabulary says beyond the landing update. This node fixes only the boundary: the registry is outside the operation vocabulary, and the landing update rides inside the recording.
